city_center.name: Downtown Houston / Buffalo Bayou
city_center.landmark: Allen's Landing at the confluence of Buffalo Bayou and White Oak Bayou -- the 1836 founding site; the Buffalo Bayou Park green corridor threads the bayou through the city
city_center.notes: Houston is the Bayou City, founded in 1836 at the confluence of Buffalo Bayou and White Oak Bayou; slow-moving bayous wind across the flat Gulf Coast plain and are called the soul of the city. sources: Houston founding at Allen's Landing (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston); Bayou City history (houstonchronicle.com); Buffalo Bayou Partnership (buffalobayou.org).

cultural_notes: Houston is the Bayou City -- founded in 1836 at the confluence of Buffalo Bayou and White Oak Bayou (Allen's Landing); the bayous are slow-moving coastal-plain waterways described as the soul of the city (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston; houstonchronicle.com Bayou City history; houstoncitybeat.com)

the flat Gulf Coast setting means the city's landscape identity is water and green corridor, not mountain -- Buffalo Bayou Park transformed the bayou into a regional outdoor amenity and flood-storage green space (source: houstonarchitecture.com Lockwood South; buffalobayou.org)

Houston is one of the most ethnically diverse metros in the US, with major Hispanic, Vietnamese, and Nigerian communities -- creative should read as multicultural, not single-heritage (INFERRED framing from region demographics -- verify community-specific claims before production)

H-E-B, including Central Market, H-E-B Plus, Joe V's Smart Shop, and Mi Tienda, leads the Houston grocery market ahead of Kroger; Joe V's and Mi Tienda are value / Hispanic-focused banners specific to this market (source: axios.com H-E-B leads Houston grocery market)
